How the detector behaves on the November recordings

5 November 2026 · Three original flight/reference recordings · RAWX + receiver sky geometry + native PX4 attitude/IMU

Exploratory replay, not a validated spoofing verdict. These recordings lack PPS edges and active TIMESYNC exchanges. Alignment uses independent receive-time envelopes with an assumed clock rate. All final validated decisions remain inconclusive. Conditional benign/spoofed outputs and γ below describe the numerical detector only. They cannot establish an alarm rate or prove a clean flight.

What this replay found

Primary run: 615 of 615 windows are inconclusive. 606 windows fail the motion-noise gate; other exclusions are native gaps and reset/calibration transitions. The 1 m/s² assumption does not permit a likelihood comparison in these windows.

The separately labelled stationary-proxy sensitivity at zero offset gives 79 benign-model preferences, 8 spoofed-model preferences and 528 inconclusive outputs. These preferences are not verified spoofing detections. Fixed ±50 ms runs show how provisional timing affects these numbers.

What was run

Unmodified detector quality thresholds and hypothesis fits, 1-second non-overlapping windows, GPS L1 C/A only (one signal per satellite), 2 cm forward antenna offset and PX4-supplied attitude. Displacement comes from our accelerometer integration; no fused PX4 displacement or GPS motion enters it.

RAWX phase/half-cycle validity, lock counters, half-cycle-subtraction changes, invalid uncertainty codes and missing samples control signal continuity. Receiver-reported NAV-SAT directions require healthy, ephemeris-source flags and age ≤2 seconds. They are approximate nominal geometry, not independently validated orbits. The recorded standard deviation scales the fit but does not calibrate real in-flight noise.

Primary acceleration white-noise assumption: 1 m/s² per sample, with the existing uncertainty gate enabled. Attitude, vibration, bias and timing errors remain outside that model. The 0 ms offset is primary; ±50 ms are fixed sensitivity checks. No timing or threshold is optimized using detector outcomes or flight labels. Windows crossing native attitude/calibration transitions are rejected.

Recording 1

20261105T131308Z_d3f681 · 299.3 seconds · 15 GPS L1 identities over the recording. 145 primary windows have an airborne midpoint; green plot shading marks these candidate intervals.

Primary conditional outputs: {'inconclusive': 299}. Airborne subset: {'inconclusive': 145}. Validated conclusive decisions: 0.

Median weakest-axis displacement RMS (airborne windows): 0.184 mm, versus the primary uncertainty bound 6.002 mm. This bound comes from an assumed noise level, not an in-flight calibration.

Timing and noise sensitivity — primary result unchanged

The stationary proxy is an optimistic diagnostic, not calibrated flight noise. Its orange plot markers and conditional outputs must not replace the primary result.

What must happen before a field conclusion
Record verified X20 pulse epochs against PX4 PPS edge timestamps; validate the clock mapping and latency budget. Calibrate the field IMU/phase error assumptions and validate nominal geometry. Retain quality exclusions; then rerun without exploratory clock assumptions.
